findings.title: Validator performs DB write causing double-counted block stats
findings.body: EmailValidator#validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and saves the BlockedEmail record. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, each of which runs validations, so one signup attempt updates stats twice. Validation must be side-effect free; the result is inflated match_count, misleading last_match_at, and extra writes on the validation path.

findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment loses updates
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? does record.match_count += 1 followed by record.save, a read-modify-write sequence. Concurrent signup attempts matching the same blocked email can read the same value and overwrite each other, losing counts. Use an atomic operation such as increment_counter or update_counters.

findings.title: Case-sensitive blocked email lookup allows bypass
findings.body: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) does an exact case-sensitive match, while email addresses are case-insensitive and the codebase normalizes with Email.downcase elsewhere. An address blocked as bad@spammers.org can be reused as BAD@spammers.org and should_block? will miss it. Uniqueness validation is also case-sensitive. Normalize emails to downcased stripped form on write and on lookup.

findings.title: Wrong Ember dependent key prevents rejected email UI update
findings.body: emailValidation depends on rejectedEmails.@each, but rejectedEmails is an array of primitive strings updated with pushObject. Ember requires rejectedEmails.[] to observe membership changes; bare @each observes properties of members, not addition of strings. After the server rejects an email, emailValidation does not recompute, so the field still shows as valid until the user edits the email.

findings.title: Moved whitelist/blacklist logic has no coverage
findings.body: The whitelist/blacklist domain logic was moved from User to EmailValidator, but the new spec only tests the blocked-email branch with BlockedEmail.should_block? stubbed. There is no test that email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist still accept or reject correctly, so a regression in the moved code would go unnoticed.
